# Archery at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's Team

## Event Overview
The women's team archery event was held at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London. It featured recurve bow competition, which is the only archery discipline in the Olympic Games.

## Format
- Teams consisted of 3 archers per country
- The competition followed the ranking round and knockout format typical of Olympic archery
- Teams competed in matches where arrows were scored in sets

## Gold Medal Winners: South Korea
South Korea dominated women's team archery, winning the gold medal. This was consistent with their historical dominance in Olympic archery.

## Competition Details
- The event took place at Lord's Cricket Ground in London
- Athletes competed outdoors in standard Olympic archery conditions
- The team event required coordination among three archers per team

## Notable Context
- South Korea has been a consistent powerhouse in Olympic archery
- The women's team event showcases the precision and consistency required at the elite level
- Team events emphasize not just individual skill but also the collective performance of all three teammates

## Specific Results
I have general knowledge that South Korea won gold, but I don't have reliable specific details about the silver and bronze medalists or the exact match scores readily available without verification.
